items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Wright opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Chonnonton peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

Councillor Wright offered further thoughts on watershed governance and the recommendations of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. She offered reflections on the passing of The Honourable Murray Sinclair, and on Treaties Recognition Week.
Treaties Recognition Week takes place annually, from November 3 to 9.
This week is an opportunity to reflect on the significance of Treaties in local history and ongoing relationships with Indigenous communities.

The City of Waterloo commissioned three replica Wampum belts: The Hiawatha, The Two-Row and The Dish with One Spoon. In June, Kahlunyunti (Martin Powless) of Oneida Nation of the Thames, the artist who recreated the belts, presented the belts to Council and provided some teaching on their history.

These belts are a physical representation of the oral history of treaties and settlement of the area around the Great Lakes Region extending along a portion of the St. Lawrence River, which we call home. These are significant representations of our colonial history and are still seen today as a reminder to all of us of the responsibilities we hold as treaty people.
The Wampum belts are currently on display in the lobby of Waterloo City Hall.

As we continue to reflect on Treaty rights and relationships, we must commit to honouring these agreements and understanding their impact on the lives of Indigenous peoples today. This is essential for Reconciliation and ensuring that Indigenous voices are recognized and respected in discussions that affect their rights and territories.
Together, we can build a future grounded in respect and collaboration between Indigenous and non-Indigenous communities.

The Hiawatha Wampum (year 1100 approx.): Depicts and describes the formation of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy under a pledge of peace and understanding between the five nations comprising the Seneca, Cayuga, Onondaga, Oneida and Mohawk tribes.
The Two-Row Wampum (year 1613 approx.): Describes the relationship between the incoming colonizing peoples and Indigenous peoples.
Specifically, between the Mohawks and the Dutch colonizers, moving forward together in parallel, but never merging, signifying respect for each other’s rights.

The Dish with One Spoon Wampum (year 1701 but could be the same age as Hiawatha Wampum): Describes an agreement for sharing hunting territory among two or more First Nation. There is a recognition that all Peoples are eating out of a single dish, that is, all hunting in the shared territory. One spoon signifies that all Peoples sharing the territory are expected to limit the game they take to leave enough for others and for the continued abundance and viability of the hunting grounds into the future.

items.title: 2023-2026 Strategic Plan – 2024
notes: Progress Report
Report No.: CAO2024-026
Prepared By: Sandy Little

Sandy Little gave a presentation with an update on the Strategic Plan progress, with an overview of the Strategic Plan, and some of work they’ve done over the last year including the Community Conversations both with staff as well as with community members. She also provided Council with some next steps, including measuring progress and the implementation of business plan initiatives. She then responded to questions of Council. Filipa Reynolds also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2024 Highlights from GRAAC
notes: Report No.: CTTEE2024-002
Prepared By: Tamara Cooper and Alyssa Clelland
Tamara Cooper, Co-Chair and Alyssa Clelland, Co-Chair gave a presentation outlining the committee overview and the highlights of their work over the last year.

Amy Ross gave a presentation and spoke about the advocacy and challenges GRAAC has faced over the past 20 years, and congratulated the committee on their hard work and dedication. Councillor Hanmer offered further remarks on the 20th Anniversary.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer offered a shout out to Community Services staff. This past weekend, October 31-November 3, the City hosted a girls’ hockey tournament in many facilities with 78 teams. Ward 4 also had a craft show at RIM Park on November 2, and hosted Community Conversations. Councillor Hanmer offered a special thanks to Moses Springer staff for going above and beyond during a hockey game.

Councillor Roach mentioned a martial arts club on Parkside Drive, Shamuon Generation of Martial Arts, who participated in the World Karate Championships in Portugal from October 26-November 1. Several club members came back with medals. He highlighted their phenomenal work with kids, improving their confidence.

Mayor McCabe attended the kickoff for MADD Canada, Mothers Against Impaired Driving, on Friday November 1. She wanted to remind everyone of the red ribbon campaign, and to be responsible over the season of many holidays.
